jobs.occupation: Manufacturing Engineer
jobs.description:
Manufacturing Engineer| Norican

Are you curious about how complex machines are built, and do you enjoy turning technical details into practical solutions on the shop floor? At DISA, we design and produce world-class foundry machines, and our team plays a key role in bringing them to life. We are looking for a Manufacturing Engineer who wants to learn, contribute and grow in a hands-on manufacturing environment.

Why you’ll love working with us

• A hands-on learning role where you work close to the product, the people and the daily assembly process.

• The chance to make a visible difference by supporting better documentation, smoother workflows and practical improvements.

• A supportive team environment where curiosity, structure and willingness to learn are just as important as years of experience.

What you’ll do

• Support the maintenance of Bill of Material (BoM), drawings and production documentation.

• Help ensure correct data, routing and set-up in our ERP system, Microsoft Dynamics 365 FO.

• Assist with production-specific configurations and learn how they enable machine production.

• Contribute to manufacturing engineering tasks in machine-specific projects together with more experienced colleagues.

• Support continuous improvement activities and learn to use Lean tools in a practical production setting.

• Work closely with shop floor colleagues to understand challenges and help turn observations into clear actions.

Who you are

• You have a BSc or MSc in Mechanical Engineering, Production Technology, Manufacturing Engineering or a similar technical field.

• You are interested in manufacturing, assembly processes and how technical documentation supports efficient production.

• You may have some experience with ERP systems such as Microsoft Dynamics 365 FO, but most importantly you are comfortable working with data and systems.

• You are curious about product configurators, production set-up and continuous improvement, and you are motivated to build your skills.

• You communicate well in English and Danish.

• You enjoy being close to the shop floor and working with people across functions to solve practical challenges.

• You are structured, detail-oriented and eager to learn – with the follow-through to turn small improvements into real progress.

What we offer

• A development-oriented role where you can grow your manufacturing engineering skills step by step.

• Access to experienced colleagues, complex products and a production environment where learning happens close to the real work.

• Competitive employment terms, including pension plan, private health insurance, catered canteen and flexible work schedule.

Why you should join Norican?

We are Norican, a global industrial group designing, building and supporting best-in-class machines and technologies for metal formation and surface treatment.

Bringing together five leading brands — DISA, Simpson, StrikoWestofen, Wheelabrator and Monitizer — we deliver one connected solution across the production process, supported by full-service expertise and digital solutions.

Across green sand molding, die casting, sand preparation, melting, transport and dosing, and surface treatment, we help manufacturers improve performance and transform production across a wide range of industries. We build lifetime quality and long-term partnerships by combining the strengths of our legacy brands to lead the industry through innovation, sustainability and profitable growth.

DISA:

DISA designs, builds and supports premium green sand moulding and casting machines for the ferrous and non-ferrous foundry industries. For 125 years, DISA has delivered machines that last for decades and is highly respected by customers and peers for excellent levels of quality and service. DISA machines keep customers producing relentlessly to the highest standards and empower foundry productivity with lifetime efficiency and a lower cost per casting.

Want to know more? Ready to apply?

Ready to learn more and ready to apply?

We review applications and conduct interviews on an ongoing basis. We will process your application confidentially, and it will only be shared with your prior consent. If you have any further questions about the position, feel free to contact our Recruitment Consultant on this role Mille Maegaard-Fast at +45 92 92 08 53.

jobs.occupation: Product & UX Consultant
jobs.description:
We're looking for a curious and entrepreneurial Product & UX Consultant who loves understanding people, challenging assumptions and turning insights into innovative products, services and experiences.

We are looking for a Product & UX Consultant

Hi there,

We're looking for a Product & UX Consultant to join our Copenhagen team and help us create even better digital products and experiences for our clients.

You'll work at the intersection of business, design and technology, helping clients understand their challenges, explore new opportunities and turn ideas into meaningful solutions. We're looking for someone who combines strategic thinking with a hands-on approach, enjoys working closely with clients and isn't afraid to take ownership and drive projects forward.

As part of our Consulting team, you'll work closely with designers, developers and strategists, taking responsibility for the user experience throughout the process. You'll also play an important role in growing our Product & UX practice at Signifly.

Danish and English at a high level is preferred.

What you'll be doing

• 
Product Strategy & Innovation: Help clients understand their challenges, identify opportunities and develop new product and service concepts that create value for users and businesses.

• 
User Research & Insights: Plan and conduct user interviews, usability tests and other research activities. Turn findings into clear insights and actionable recommendations.

• 
UX Design & Concept Development: Translate insights and ideas into user journeys, flows, wireframes and prototypes that help bring solutions to life.

• 
Service Design: Explore and improve end-to-end service experiences across physical and digital touchpoints, considering the people, processes and interactions that shape the overall experience.

• 
Workshops & Facilitation: Plan and facilitate workshops with clients, users and stakeholders to explore challenges, develop ideas and align on solutions.

• 
Client Collaboration & Project Ownership: Take ownership of projects and workstreams, challenge clients' thinking and work closely with designers, developers and strategists to create great solutions.

• 
Growing Product & UX at Signifly: Help us develop our methods, challenge existing approaches and build an even stronger Product & UX practice.

What we expect of you

To be considered for this position, we imagine that you have:

• 
Hands on experience in digital product development, UX, service design or consulting.

• 
A strong understanding of user-centred design and how to balance user needs, business objectives and technology to create meaningful solutions.

• 
The ability to combine creative exploration with analytical and structured thinking, translating complex challenges and research findings into clear recommendations and concepts.

• 
A hands-on approach to problem-solving, with experience in research, concept development and preferably wireframing or prototyping.

• 
The confidence to take ownership, drive projects forward, facilitate workshops and challenge clients and colleagues when needed.

• 
A collaborative mindset and experience with stakeholder management. You enjoy working with designers, developers, strategists and business stakeholders.

• 
An entrepreneurial mindset. Maybe you've built something yourself, worked in a startup or thought about starting your own business a million times?

• 
You're comfortable using emerging tools and technologies, including AI, to accelerate research, explore ideas and improve the way we work.

We don't expect you to be an expert in everything. You might come from a background in business, digital product development, UX or service design. Most importantly, we're looking for someone who takes initiative, thinks critically and genuinely cares about creating better products and experiences for people.

What you can expect from us

We offer an ambitious yet down-to-earth work environment with a focus on learning, collaboration, and personal growth.

Plus, a few perks:

• 
Annual, paid team trip (Italy, Portugal in past years and soon Canada).

• 
Fresh catered lunch (mostly organic, vegetarian options available).

• 
Unlimited snacks & drinks (including Friday wine & beers).

• 
Beautiful office at Vesterbro Torv.

• 
High-quality equipment - you choose what you prefer.

• 
In-office massage service.

• 
Paid inspiration trips (events, meetups, conferences).

• 
Company-paid pension and health insurance.

• 
Competitive salary based on qualifications and performance.

• 
Merit-based career progression - your impact matters more than seniority.

• 
Work-exchange opportunities in Montreal, Toronto, or London.

And if something’s missing? Let us know.

Ready to do the best work of your career?

Then don’t hesitate to send us your application and CV or online profile (LinkedIn or GitHub) – and feel free to include links to projects you’re proud of. Then we will be in touch! Applications are reviewed continuously as we receive them, and we hire when we find the right candidate.  For more information or questions please contact us at job@signifly.com

jobs.occupation: Senior HR Business Partner
jobs.description:
– Hands-on HR business partnering driving business transformation and performance improvement

Partner with executives and senior leaders to support business transformation and integration, strengthen organisational and leadership capabilities and improve business performance through hands-on HR business partnering.

Our client is a leading provider of project-based green services across Denmark and is part of an international group. Its clients include municipalities, businesses, infrastructure operators, housing associations and private clients.

Your role

This newly created role is embedded in a business unit (BU) of approximately 300 employees across several locations in Denmark. You will combine strategic HR advice with hands-on, business-oriented HR delivery, helping the BU become a stronger, more integrated and performance-oriented business.

A key priority is to strengthen the BU’s HR foundations, helping leaders lead people more effectively and putting agreed HR processes into practice.

You will report directly to the executive leader accountable for the BU, with functional dotted-line reporting to the Danish CEO and Group CHRO. You will be a member of both the BU leadership team and the Group HR leadership team.

Key responsibilities

• 
Support the BU’s transformation and integration through organisation design and effective change execution. Clarify accountabilities, strengthen collaboration within the BU and help leaders take greater ownership of people management.

• 
Assess organisational and leadership capabilities, assess and map talent, map succession options and identify critical capability gaps. Translate findings into practical organisational, leadership and talent development actions.

• 
Support the people and organisational aspects of the planned merger of the BU’s legal entities into a single legal entity as one of the BU’s major transformation projects.

• 
Provide advice and hands-on HR support to the executive leader accountable for the BU and the BU’s leaders on organisational decisions, workforce requirements and day-to-day people matters.

• 
Plan, facilitate and follow up on the BU’s agreed annual HR processes, including salary reviews, performance management and talent reviews. Help leaders set clear expectations, provide feedback and address performance and development needs.

• 
Strengthen workforce planning, recruitment, retention and talent development. Work with colleagues on employer branding, apprenticeships and educational partnerships.

• 
Support employee engagement and a shared culture through employee dialogue, effective change communication and follow-up on engagement survey findings, with clear leadership ownership of actions.

• 
Support compliance with Danish employment law and collective agreements in collaboration with Legal, Finance and relevant specialists.

• 
Participate in Group HR leadership team meetings and coordinate agreed Group HR activities with HR colleagues supporting the different Danish businesses.

You will also support agreed preparations for greater pay transparency and work with business leaders and IT on potential initiatives involving a new HR system, digitalisation and AI. Any implementation will depend on agreed priorities and budget.

What you bring

You bring at least five years’ experience in HR business partnering or a comparable business-facing role, combining commercial judgement with hands-on delivery.

Your background includes:

• 
Experience supporting business transformation and integration, organisation design and effective change execution.

• 
Experience assessing organisational and leadership capabilities, assessing talent, mapping talent and succession options and translating assessment findings into practical organisational and development actions.

• 
Experience delivering annual HR processes, including salary reviews, performance management and talent reviews, alongside workforce planning and recruitment.

• 
Sound knowledge of Danish employment law and practical experience with collective agreements, employee representatives and complex employee matters.

• 
Strong stakeholder and project management skills, including advising senior leaders, working internationally and coordinating with HR colleagues on agreed HR initiatives.

• 
Ability to deliver agreed priorities within available resources and use people data to inform decisions and measure progress.

• 
Ability to work with business leaders and IT on the people and organisational change aspects of implementing and adopting HR systems, digital tools and AI; specialist technical expertise is not required.

You hold a relevant higher education qualification in HR, business administration, psychology, strategy, management or similar and have strong written and spoken communication skills in Danish and English.

Experience in construction, project-based services or a business with operational teams across several locations would be an advantage.

You build trust at all levels through sound judgement, clear communication and consistent follow-through. You work independently, collaborate effectively and balance longer-term development with day-to-day people matters. You enjoy a busy, varied working environment and remain effective through change and uncertainty.

Why consider this opportunity?

As a member of both the BU leadership team and the Group HR leadership team, you will work directly with decision-makers and help shape the BU’s next stage of development. You will strengthen the BU’s HR foundations and organisational and leadership capabilities and see how your work contributes to improved business performance. Collaboration with colleagues across an international group provides opportunities to exchange expertise and develop professionally.

Location and travel

The position is based on Zealand, west of Copenhagen, with approximately three days per week at the main office and regular travel to other BU locations in Denmark. The precise attendance and travel arrangements will be agreed.

Interested?

Please submit your CV and application via the application link by 10 December 2026. Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis, with selected candidates invited to an initial online interview with Brinch & Partners. First-round presentations to our client are provisionally scheduled for mid-December:

• Tuesday, 15 December 2026

• Thursday, 17 December 2026

• Friday, 18 December 2026

For a confidential conversation about this opportunity, please contact Heidi Lindeholm Fogtmann, Partner at Brinch & Partners, on +45 2679 3252 or hlf@brinchpartners.dk.

We welcome applications from qualified candidates of all backgrounds.

jobs.description:
Vi søger dig, der brænder for relationsarbejde og ønsker at gøre en mærkbar forskel for et menneske i en meget sårbar livssituation.
Du bliver en del af et dedikeret team omkring borgeren, hvor din faglighed, ro og evne til at skabe tillid er helt afgørende. 

 
Lidt om borgeren .. 

Borger er en ældre, reflekteret og intellektuel mand med erhvervet hjerneskade. Han har levet et rigt liv – bl.a. med interesse for livsstil, filosofi, natur og alternativ behandling – han bærer stadig en stærk personlighed og behov for at blive mødt med respekt og ægthed.

Samtidig er han i en livssituation præget af:

• Udbredt angst og utryghed ved at være alene
• Kognitive udfordringer (bl.a. hukommelse og impulskontrol)
• Behov for tydelig, rolig og respektfuld kommunikation
Borger har brug for en medarbejder, der:

• Er nærværende og i dialog – det er helt centralt for ham
• Taler med ham – ikke til eller ned til ham
• Skaber tryghed ved at forklare alt, der sker (fx “nu løfter jeg din arm”)
• Kan rumme frustrationer og et skarpt toneleje uden at miste roen
Når relationen er stærk, trives borger bedst – og det er her, du gør den største forskel.

 
Din rolle

Du bliver en fast del af et team på 3 medarbejdere og vil arbejde tæt med borger i en 1:1-indsats, hvor opgaven blandt andet indeholder:

• Fuld personlig pleje og daglig omsorg - herunder lift og bleskift
• Støtte til måltider (både fysisk og verbal guidning)
• Arbejde med tryghed og relation som fundament
• Gradvis træning af borgers evne til at være alene
• Low arousal-tilgang i praksis
• Dokumentation i Nexus (døgnrytmeskema, uroregistrering, livshistorie) samt i Olivia Danmarks journalsystem Heretask.
Derudover vil du – når det er muligt – indgå i den øvrige drift på plejecentret og blive en del af et stærkt team. 
Kollegaer i teamet vil sikre god oplæring, så du er klædt på til opgaven og du vil få 2-3 følge vagter inden en selvstændig vagt. 

 
Vi søger dig som .. 

Er mere end din faglighed – du er en person, man kan læne sig op ad i mødet med et menneske i krise.
Vi forestiller os, at du:

• Er SSA, SSH eller ufaglært med solid erfaring inden for pleje og omsorgsområdet
• Har erfaring med eller interesse for hjerneskadeområdet
• Arbejder roligt, tydeligt og relationsorienteret
• Trives med tæt borgerkontakt og komplekse opgaver
• Er sprogligt stærk, tydelig i din kommunikation og grænsesættende
• Kan skabe struktur, forudsigelighed og tryghed
• Har forståelse for low arousal og betydningen af en god relation
Du kan møde et menneske dér, hvor mennesket er – og se personen bag skaden.

 
Derfor skal du vælge netop denne stilling ..

• Du får mulighed for at arbejde helt tæt med ét menneske og gøre en konkret forskel
• Du bliver en del af et fagligt funderet og dedikeret team
• Du arbejder med en kompleks og udviklende opgave, hvor relationen er i centrum
• Du får mulighed for at bruge både dine faglige og menneskelige kompetencer fuldt ud
 

Arbejdstid:
Du vil indgå i et 4 ugers rul sammen med resten af teamet - dine arbejdstider vil være følgende:

You will be the microbiologist in a team of medicinal chemists and infectious disease specialists, collaborating on developing new solutions for patients with chronic biofilm infections. The NNF-funded project aims to achieve this through targeted delivery of enzyme conjugates that latch on to the biofilm and degrade the extracellular matrix. You will contribute to design and in vitro evaluation in biofilm models, using an array of advanced microscopy, molecular and biochemical analyses.

Your profile
You are a highly driven scientist with a PhD in microbiology or similar and with research experience in microbial biofilms, advanced microscopy or microorganisms, or evaluation of antimicrobial therapies.
You have published in peer-reviewed journals and can take the lead in writing research publications. You enjoy working in an international and interdisciplinary team where research activities and publication of results involve multiple research groups.

Who we are
You will be affiliated with the research group of Rikke Meyer (https://bio.au.dk/en/research/research-areas/microbial-processes-and-diversity/biofilm-group) at the Department of Biology, Section for Microbiology. The labs are located at the university campus in a cross-departmental research facility housing research groups from biology, molecular biology, chemistry, physics and nanoscience. You will also be part of the vibrant research community at the Section for Microbiology ( https://bio.au.dk/en/about-biology/sections/microbiology).

What we offer

• a well-developed research infrastructure, laboratories and access to shared equipment

• a work environment with close working relationships, networking and social activities

This is a two-year position from 1 March or as soon as possible.

Contact information

jobs.description:
We are looking for a highly motivated and dynamic assistant in AI for infectious disease with experience in machine learning, pathogen evolutionary modelling, and clinical registry data for a 4-year position commencing on 1 March 2027.

The position involves developing large language models, multimodal models and benchmarks for pathogen analysis within the Global Pathogen Analysis Platform (GPAP). The candidate must therefore combine strong machine learning skills with experience working with pathogen or infectious disease data.

Information on the department can be found at ifsv.ku.dk.

Our research
The Section of Health Data Science and AI actively contributes to advancing health data analysis, with a particular emphasis on computational tools for advanced decision making in policy and the clinic. Our research explores the dynamic interactions among genes, pathogens, the environment, and health throughout the life course and across generations. As an Assistant Professor, you would become a member of The Computational and Mathematical Global Health Group, co-led by Professor Samir Bhatt and Associate Professor David Duchene, located at the Department of Public Health of the University of Copenhagen. We are a world-leading group that focuses on a diverse range of topics. We research at the interface of computer science, mathematics, biology, and epidemiology.

Your job 
The Assistant Professorship will focus on AI research within the Global Pathogen Analysis Platform (GPAP), whose mission is to develop a freely accessible platform to support infectious disease surveillance across human, animal and environmental health. In particular, we wish to advance our understanding of large language models and agentic systems for pathogen analysis. The candidate will develop multimodal models, contribute to the creation of LLM post-training datasets and build benchmarks to compare LLMs for pathogen analysis. Alongside this project, the candidate will help supervise students in applying deep learning techniques across multiple modalities (e.g., text, audio, video) for a range of public health topics. The candidate will therefore require strong background knowledge in data science, machine learning and infectious disease modelling.

The assistant professor’s responsibilities will primarily consist of: 

• 
research, including publication/academic dissemination duties

• 
research-based teaching

• 
sharing knowledge with society

• 
participation in formal pedagogical training programme for assistant professors

Profile 
Five overall criteria apply for assistant professor appointments at the University of Copenhagen. The five criteria (research, teaching, innovation and societal impact, organisational contribution and leadership) are considered a framework for the overall assessment of candidates. Find information about each criterion here.

Furthermore, we are looking for a highly motivated and enthusiastic scientist with the following skills and experience:

Essential experience and skills:

• 
You have a PhD in health data science, computational biology, bioinformatics or a related quantitative field.

• 
You are highly experienced in analysing pathogen data (e.g., phylogenetics, pathogen genomics), documented by first-author peer-reviewed publications.

• 
You are highly experienced in deep learning across data modalities (biological sequences, protein structures, text, audio, video) and have experience with large language models (e.g., fine-tuning, evaluation or benchmarking).

• 
You are highly experienced in Python and research software engineering, including unit testing, version control, and collaborative development, documented by open-source software you have developed and maintained.

• 
You have an active interest in mathematical modelling of evolutionary processes and applying computational methods to public health challenges.

• 
You have pre- and postgraduate teaching experience within data science, programming or machine learning

• 
Proficient communication skills and ability to work in teams.

• 
Excellent English skills written and spoken.

 Desirable experience and skills:

Experience in grant writing and application.

Knowledge of advanced regression modelling implemented in a Bayesian framework.

• 
Demonstrated experience in clinical machine learning.

Experience with phylogenetic inference and its applications, e.g., phylodynamics, molecular evolution or comparative analysis.

Experience supervising students or interns.

Experience collaborating with public health authorities, hospitals or national registries.

Place of employment

jobs.occupation: Afdelingsleder med særlig interesse for børn med specifikke indlæringsvanskeligheder
jobs.description:
Sct. Jacobi Skole og Dagtilbud søger en leder med hjerte for specialområdet og engagement i at skabe de bedste rammer for børnene på vores særlige X-spor i indskolingen og på mellemtrinnet. Børnene har specifikke indlæringsvanskeligheder, herunder ADHD.

Søg jobbet, hvis du brænder for at: 

• Gøre en reel forskel for børn og unge med særlige behov 
• Udvikle spændende og alternative læringsfælleskaber, der styrker børnenes motivation og deltagelsesmuligheder
• Sætte dit præg og være med til at relancere specialområdet 
• Bliver en del af et nyt ledelsesteam, hvor vi tør stille spørgsmål til vores praksis og udvikle den i fællesskab
Som afdelingsleder får du ansvaret for den daglige ledelse af vores afdeling for børn, der på grund af forskellige indlæringsvanskeligheder har brug for en særlig struktur for at folde deres fulde potentiale ud. Vi tror på, at alle børn gør det, så godt de kan, og vi hjælper kærligt til, så alle får mulighed for at blive en del af fællesskabet. 

Vi arbejder med struktur, visuel støtte og relationsarbejde, så alle børn kan deltage og udvikle sig i sit eget tempo. 
Sct. Jacobi Skole og Dagtilbud 

Vi har ca. 270 elever fra 0.-10. klasse og omkring 180 engagerede medarbejdere. Skolen er fordelt på tre matrikler: Pramstedvej og Laboratorievej i Varde og i Tistrup. 

På Sct. Jacobi træder du ind i en organisation med høj faglighed, engagerede medarbejdere og et veletableret tværprofessionelt samarbejde, hvor forskellige perspektiver og kompetencer ses som en styrke.

Her får du mulighed for både faglig fordybelse og personlig udvikling som leder. Du kommer til at arbejde i en organisation, der bygger på en systemisk og ressourceorienteret tilgang, og hvor udvikling, læring og stærke relationer er fundamentet for vores arbejde. Hvis du motiveres af at udvikle mennesker, skabe stærke faglige fællesskaber og omsætte ambitioner til meningsfuld praksis, kan dette være dit næste lederjob. 
Vores børnesyn og pædagogiske grundlag 

I samarbejde med forældrene og andre samarbejdspartnere arbejder vi for at skabe rammerne for et godt børne- og ungdomsliv, hvor børn og unge med generelle og specifikke indlæringsvanskeligheder udvikler livsstrategier, som sigter mod inklusion i det almindelige fællesskab. Med andre ord skaber vi sammen fremtidens voksne. 

Vi tager afsæt i et fælles pædagogisk grundlag, hvor vi tror på, at alle børn har superkræfter. Vi ser ikke barnet som sin diagnose, men som et menneske med evner, ressourcer og muligheder, der kan udfoldes og udvikles. 
Ledelse er noget vi skaber sammen

Som afdelingsleder bliver du en del af skolens ledelsesteam, der består af 6 afdelingsledere, en viceskoleleder og en skoleleder. Vi arbejder ud fra princippet om fælles ledelse og fælles ansvar. Derfor forventer vi, at du aktivt bidrager til udviklingen af hele organisationen, samtidig med at du tager ansvar for egne ledelsesområder. 

Vi er et nyt lederteam, så du kan være med til at præge den kultur, vi skaber sammen. Det ligger dog fast, at vi vil videreføre vores ledelse, der bygger på tillid, mod, nysgerrighed, ordentlighed og stærke relationer. Vi støtter og udfordrer hinanden, og vi tror på, at de bedste løsninger opstår i et tæt samarbejde mellem ledere, medarbejdere og samarbejdspartnere. 

Du passer perfekt ind som leder hos os, hvis du brænder for specialområdet og meget gerne har viden om specifikke indlæringsvanskeligheder som fx ADHD, oppositionel adfærdsforstyrrelse og tilknytningsforstyrrelse. 

Vi regner med, at du har en relevant uddannelsesbaggrund og nogle års ledelseserfaring. Desuden håber vi, at du:

• Motiveres af personaleledelse og at skabe ejerskab gennem medinddragelse og naturligt inddrager medarbejdernes professionelle dømmekraft 
• Har et anerkendende, ressourceorienteret og udviklingsorienteret menneskesyn 
• Har erfaring med at skabe stærke relationer og kan bidrage til det gode samarbejde med medarbejdere, forældre og eksterne aktører.  
• Viser mod, integritet og handlekraft i dine opgaver og ledelsesbeslutninger 
Vil du vide mere?

Hvis du er blevet nysgerrig og gerne vil høre mere om jobbet, så ring endelig til skoleleder Toke Knudsmark på telefon 21 31 50 73. 

Du kan også læse mere om os på vores hjemmeside, og her kan du se vores pædagogiske grundlag.

Din ansøgning 

Du behøver ikke skrive en klassisk ansøgning. Send os i stedet dit CV sammen med dette: 

• en beskrivelse af din motivation for netop dette lederjob
• dit bud på, hvilke elementer du ser som særligt vigtige for succesfuld organisatorisk udvikling af et nyt ledelsesteam
Hvis du har lyst til at komme med på holdet, så send os endelig din ansøgning senest den 3. januar 2027. Vi forventer at afholde ansættelsessamtaler 14.01 og 21.01 2027.

Tiltrædelse forventes 1. marts 2027 eller snarest muligt. Før du indstilles til ansættelse, indhenter vi referencer og børneattest.

Vi glæder os meget til at høre fra dig.

jobs.occupation: Senior Process Engineer – Materials Characterisation (FIB & TEM), NNF Quantum Computing Programme
jobs.description:
The Novo Nordisk Foundation Quantum Computing Programme (NQCP) is establishing a talented and diverse international team to create a cutting-edge quantum programme in the heart of Copenhagen, Denmark. At the Niels Bohr Institute, University of Copenhagen, where the formulation of Quantum Mechanics was born 100 years ago, we aim to establish an international quantum computing programme, generously funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation, that will drive research and innovations at multiple levels - from developing scalable quantum processor technologies to solutions for the quantum-classical control and readout interface, and all the way to quantum algorithms and applications.  The long-term mission of the programme is to develop fault-tolerant quantum computing hardware and quantum algorithms that solve life-science-relevant chemical and biological problems.

  The role:

  The NQCP Materials team is looking for a senior process engineer to drive the structural characterisation of novel solid-state materials for quantum computing. You will be the teams lead expert for focused ion beam (FIB) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). As a senior member of a small, fast-moving team, you will also contribute more broadly to the team's characterisation and process needs as the programme evolves.

  Your FIB and TEM responsibilities will include:

   	
• Preparing high-quality TEM lamellae and cross-sections by FIB, including site-specific lift-out from complex heterostructures, thin films and nanoscale devices 	
• Performing advanced TEM/STEM characterisation of crystal structure, defects, interfaces and composition 	
• Developing, standardising and automating FIB and TEM workflows to ensure reliable, reproducible and precise extraction of relevant materials metrics 	
• Training other users in the operation of the FIB and TEM, and taking responsibility for best practices, instrument documentation and safe, efficient use of the instruments 	
• Coordinating and distributing TEM tasks with external collaborators 	
• Feeding results back to colleagues in materials growth and nanofabrication to guide process development   Beyond FIB and TEM, you will:

   	
• Contribute to and perform other characterisation techniques used by the team (e.g. SEM, AFM, XRD or XPS) and help integrate them with FIB/TEM results into a coherent picture of materials quality 	
• Take part in shared team tasks such as instrument operation and maintenance, data infrastructure, and the planning and prioritisation of characterisation work 	
• Engage with new methods and responsibilities as the needs of the programme develop   You'll be part of a hands-on, collaborative and deeply interdisciplinary environment, with colleagues who have expertise in materials growth, nanofabrication, various characterisation techniques, and theory and simulation, as well as international partners from industry and academia.

  Professional and personal qualifications

  Your qualifications include:

   	
• Master's or PhD in physics, materials science, chemical engineering or a related field 	
• At least 5 years of hands-on academic or industrial experience with FIB and TEM as your primary techniques 	
• Extensive experience with FIB lamella preparation, including lift-out, thinning and low-damage final polishing 	
• Strong expertise in TEM/STEM techniques such as HRTEM, HAADF-STEM, electron diffraction and analytical methods (EDS and/or EELS), as well as the associated data analysis 	
• Experience training and supervising other instrument users 	
• Deep understanding of the properties of materials and their underlying structures, including interfaces and defects 	
• Experience with scripting for automation, data logging and data processing, as well as systems engineering concepts 	
• Experience with SEM, AFM, XRD, XPS or nanofabrication is a strong advantage 	
• Willingness and motivation to take on responsibilities beyond your core techniques and to learn new skills 	
• Good communication skills and the ability to coordinate work in a complex research programme   You are driven and self-motivated, keep focused on pace and outcome, and inspire others with your constructive and collaborative workstyle. Your colleagues would describe you as analytical, structured and curious. You are a team player who takes ownership of the team's shared goals and works to develop the best solutions with input from highly skilled colleagues in interdisciplinary fields.

  Why us?
 By joining NQCP now, you will be involved from the very beginning and contribute to fulfilling its mission. We want to make Denmark a world leader in quantum research, and we hope to attract people from all over the world.

  Life in Denmark is supported by strong social services: free universal healthcare, free or subsidised language courses, paid parental leave, subsidised day care and excellent public schools. Our work culture is very egalitarian and prioritises work-life balance. Dual-career families are the norm, and workplaces offer flexibility so everyone can have both an exciting career and good family time. Danish cities are known for excellent infrastructure, such as widespread bike path networks, and we can also offer a thriving food scene, excellent museums and beautiful natural scenery.

  Terms of salary and employment
 The employment and salary are in accordance with the Circular on the Collective Agreement concerning academics in the state sector, concluded between the Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations).

  Employment will be as special consultant. The salary is based on seniority, and negotiation for a salary supplement is possible. The working time is 37 hours per week on average, and working hours are flexible. The position is limited in time until 31 December 2029.

  Appointment is subject to receipt of a security clearance.

  When you will be affiliated with the University of Copenhagen or otherwise have access to their research, you may be required to undergo a background screening. The purpose is to protect the security and research integrity of the University of Copenhagen.

  Your application
 If you find this position interesting, please send an electronic application with attachments via Jobportalen (click "Apply Now" at the bottom of this post) no later than 12 December 2026.

  Please include:

   	
• Curriculum vitae, including a short cover letter 	
• Diplomas (Master's and PhD degree or equivalent) 	
• Publication list (if relevant)   Further information
 For further information, please contact Asbjørn Drachmann (asbjorn.drachmann@nbi.ku.dk).

  The Faculty of Science at the University of Copenhagen (SCIENCE) is Denmark's largest science research and education institution, with 4,000 employees and 9,700 Bachelor's and Master's students in 12 departments. The faculty has an annual budget of DKK 3 billion. Learn more at www.science.ku.dk.

jobs.description:
Lead a national photonics and quantum technology infrastructure from concept to operation

At DTU Nanolab, we are looking for an experienced and highly motivated project manager to lead the establishment of PHODESIK (Photonic Process Design Kit), a major national research infrastructure initiative within photonics and quantum technologies.

PHODESIK is part of the Danish Roadmap for Research Infrastructure (NUFI) and brings together DTU, Danish universities, research institutions, and industry partners to establish a national platform for advanced photonic and quantum photonic technologies. In this role, you will coordinate a complex multi-partner project and play a key role in ensuring that the technical, organizational, and strategic objectives of the initiative are successfully delivered.

Leading a National Research Infrastructure Initiative
PHODESIK is a national research infrastructure initiative on the Danish Roadmap for Research Infrastructure (NUFI). The project aims to establish a national platform for the design, fabrication, characterization, and deployment of advanced photonic and quantum photonic devices, where researchers and companies can move from photonic circuit design to a reproducible fabricated devices in a Process Design Kit driven fabrication flow. The infrastructure combines state-of-the-art nanofabrication facilities at DTU Nanolab with characterization capabilities at Danish universities and a digital Process Design Kit (PDK) framework developed together with DFM.

As project manager, you will be responsible for coordinating activities across the PHODESIK consortium and ensure successful implementation of a large-scale infrastructure project involving researchers, technical specialists, university partners, industrial stakeholders, and equipment suppliers.

Our expectations of you
Technical insight combined with strong stakeholder and project management skills.

We expect you to have:

• A relevant master’s degree or PhD in photonics, nanotechnology, or a related discipline.
• Demonstrated experience managing complex technical or research-related projects.
• Experience working with multiple stakeholders across research institutions, industry, and public organizations.
• Strong organizational and planning skills with the ability to drive activities across diverse teams.
• Excellent communication skills and the ability to translate technical challenges into actionable plans.
It will be considered an advantage if you have:

• Experience with photonic integrated circuits, PICs
• Knowledge of photonics, semiconductor technologies, nanofabrication, quantum technologies, or research infrastructures.
• Experience with scientific facilities, advanced instrumentation, or technology implementation projects.
• Experience with public procurement, infrastructure acquisition, or project governance in publicly funded projects.
• Familiarity with digital platforms, interoperability principles, and data integration.
As a person, you:

Department of Geosciences and Natural Resource Management, Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen

  Within the European Union’s Horizon Europe research and innovation programme under the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Action (MSCA), University of Copenhagen is offering a 1-year Research Assistant (RA) position starting 1 April 2027 (or as soon as possible thereafter), which then leads to a 3-year PhD fellowship for a Doctoral Candidate (DC).

  The combined position is part of the research project STEP-UP (Safe, Thriving, and Engaged Pedestrians in Urban Public Spaces), which is funded by the European Union’s Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA), Doctoral Networks (DN), Call: HORIZON-MSCA-2025-DN-01.

  The STEP-UP network supports 10 PhD Candidates in investigating pedestrian behaviour and mobility in urban environments.

  The 10 PhD projects are closely linked, contributing complementary perspectives to a shared research agenda in three areas: individual and interpersonal aspects of pedestrian behaviour, environmental and infrastructural barriers to walking, and interactions between pedestrians and other road users. The aim is to improve the understanding of pedestrian mobility and support the development of safer and more inclusive urban public spaces.

  STEP-UP brings together academic and non-academic partners to train 10 doctoral candidates through an international Joint Doctorate programme. The candidates benefit from joint supervision by researchers at partner institutions, an integrated doctoral training programme, and opportunities for interdisciplinary and cross-sectoral collaboration, including research secondments at partner organisations. In addition to specialised scientific knowledge, they develop transferable skills in areas such as research communication and dissemination. The programme prepares them for careers in research and other fields related to transport and urban development.

  For a description of the STEP-UP project and descriptions of all 10 PhD positions, please visit the STEP-UP project’s website https://www.project-stepup.eu/

  STEP-UP is based on 4-year double PhD degree programs. This means that the successful applicant will also be enrolled in a partner university’s PhD programme.

  Job and project description
 The RA position will entail carrying out a literature review of the research field, identifying current research gaps, and preparing for data collection. 

  The PhD position will entail carrying out the research activities of the research project as described below.

  Your key tasks as a PhD fellow at the Faculty of SCIENCE are to:

   	
• Conduct an independent research project under supervision. 	
• Complete PhD courses or other equivalent education corresponding to approximately 30 ECTS points. 	
• Participate in active research environments including a mandatory stay for a minimum of 12 months at the partner university (see below for further details). 	
• Contribute to teaching or other types of dissemination related to your PhD project (e.g., at conferences, meetings, etc.) 	
• Write a PhD thesis on the grounds of your project   About the research project
 The project “Urban space transformation projects for improved and inclusive walkability”. will investigate how planning and design approaches applied in urban space transformation projects impact pedestrians’ behaviour and perceived safety and accessibility (walkability). Urban transformation projects are increasingly proposed to respond to the evolving needs of contemporary cities. Combining urban planning and transport engineering is essential, as planning shapes the spatial and social context of urban spaces while transport engineering ensures safe, efficient and accessible movement. The PhD project will:  (1) collect data on goals and practices of urban space transformation projects; pedestrian pedestrians’ behaviours, preferences and perceptions of walkability in relation to the transformation interventions; (2) identify walkability indicators across diverse groups of pedestrians; (3) comprehensively evaluate pedestrians’ perceived impacts of current transformations for enhanced liveability and pedestrianisation; and (4) develop a methodological framework for local adaptation and upscaling of approaches for enhanced perceived walkability. Partner university: National Technical University of Athens (NTUA) Planned secondments at NTUA: M16–M24 and M37–M48.

  Pricipal supervisor: Assoc. Prof. Trine Agervig Carstensen, University of Copenhagen, email: tac@ign.ku.dk.

  Co-supervisor: Prof. Konstantinos Kepaptsoglou, National Technical University of Athens (NTUA), email: kkepap@central.ntua.gr

  Place of employment
 The primary place of employment will be Department of Geosciences and Natural Resource Management, Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in dynamic and international research environment. Our research facilities include modern laboratories and state-of-the-art hardware and software. More information on the department can be found here: https://ign.ku.dk/english/

  During the PhD programme of research the candidate will be on a secondment for minimum 12 months in total at the partner university.

  Required qualifications
 As an applicant you must have:

   	
• To be eligible for the PhD programme at UCPH, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. Urban Planning, Geography, Civil Engineering, Psychology, Architecture, Landscape Architecture, Sociology, or related-disciplines. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database. 	
• To be eligible for the PhD programme at the National University of Athens, you are required to fulfil the requirements described here: https://eur02.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.survey.ntua.gr%2Fen%2Fstudies%2Fpostgraduate%2Fdoctoral-studies&data=05%7C02%7Ctac%40ign.ku.dk%7Ce197702553f44a00a12308df44a25d10%7Ca3927f91cda14696af898c9f1ceffa91%7C0%7C0%7C639305136264965933%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=62PInKwPpyGrwa3VViUOFLlXisPlz4b7rgs6kdWwhNI%3D&reserved=0 	
• Fluency in English and excellent communications skills.    Applicants will also be required to meet the European Commission’s MSCA Doctoral Network eligibility criteria, notably:

   	
• Mobility Rule - Applicants can be of any nationality and must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Denmark for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before the start of their employment at UCPH. Compulsory national service, short stays such as holidays, and time spent as part of a procedure for obtaining refugee status under the Geneva Convention are not considered. 	
• Doctoral Candidate requirement – the applicant must not be in possession of a doctoral degree at the first day of the employment. Researchers who have successfully defended their doctoral thesis, but who have not yet been awarded the doctoral degree are not eligible.   Please note that you will only be considered for the position if you fulfil both above eligibility criteria.

  Who are we looking for?
 We are looking for candidates within the field(s) of spatial, engineering, or behavioural sciences. Applicants can have a background in Urban and Regional Planning, Geography, Civil Engineering, Architecture, Landscape Architecture, Psychology, Sociology, or related disciplines.

  The following experiences and skills will be emphasised. Applicants are encouraged to provide relevant details and supporting evidence, where applicable:

   	
• Urban design / urban planning 	
• Human-environment interactions 	
• Qualitative case study methods 	
• Data analysis / statistical analysis   Personal attributes that are desirable:

   	
• Strong motivation for high-quality research 	
• Collaborative spirit 	
• Systematic approach to research 	
• Attention to detail   Key criteria for the assessment of applicants

   	
• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD project 	
• Relevance of studies, coursework, and thesis 	
• Relevant work experience (if any) 	
• Publications (if any) 	
• The grade point average achieved 	
• Other professional activities 	
• Language skills 	
• Quality and relevance of project proposal 	
• The successful applicant is also required to be enterprising and to possess good   interpersonal skills   Terms of employment
 The arrangement concerns two separate fixed-term positions: initially as a Research Assistant, leading towards an appointment as a PhD fellow. The respective durations of the two positions are 1 year and 3 years.

  The position as a PhD fellow is contingent upon the successful enrolment of a suitable candidate in the PhD School at the University of Copenhagen, as well as satisfactory completion of the Research Assistant period. These assessments will be carried out 3-6  months prior to the expiry of the Research Assistant contract. The start date is 1 April 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The PhD study must be completed in accordance with The Ministerial Order on the PhD programme (2013) and the faculty’s rules on achieving the degree.

  Salary, pension and terms of employment are in accordance with the requirements from the European Commission related to the MSCA programme and the agreement between the Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. Depending on seniority, the monthly salary starts at approximately 31,850 DKK/roughly 4,260 EUR (August 2026 level). Depending on qualifications, a supplement may be negotiated. The employer will pay an additional 18.07 % to your pension fund. 

  Application and assessment procedure
 Your application, written in English, must be submitted electronically by clicking “Apply now” below and must include the following documents in PDF format:

   	
• Motivation letter of application (max. one page) 	
• A project proposal (max 5 pages where the candidate presents a proposal on how they wish to approach their project including theory and methods) 	
• CV incl. education, experience, language skills, publication list (if any), and other skills relevant for the position 	
• Certified copy of original master’s diploma and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorised English translation if issued in other language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted. As a prerequisite for a PhD position employment, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database. Please note that we might ask you to obtain an assessment of your education performed by the Ministry of Higher Education and Science.
 	Applicants with a master´s degree from abroad should also enclose a short description of the grading scale used.
 	Certified copy of original bachelor’s diploma and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorised English translation if issued in other language than English or Danish. If the applicant has completed a combined bachelor’s and master’s education (e.g. 5-year combined master’s), the applicant should submit the combined diploma, transcript of records, and authorised English translations if issued in other language than English or Danish. 	
• Language diplomas or language test results (if any)   The deadline for applications is 20 December 2026, at 23.59pm CET.

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process
 After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorised recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the hiring committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment by an unbiased assessor.

  The assessor makes a non-prioritised assessment of the academic qualifications and experience with respect to the above-mentioned area of research, techniques, skills and other requirements listed in the advertisement.

  Once the assessment work has been completed, each applicant can comment on the part of the assessment that relates to him/herself.

  The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

  You may read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

  For more information on working and living in Denmark visit http://ism.ku.dk (International Staff Mobility) and https://www.workindenmark.dk.

  Interviews are expected to take place in the beginning of February 2027.

  Questions
 For specific information about the PhD position, please contact the principal supervisor, Trine Agervig Carstensen.

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the diversity of society and encourages all qualified candidates to apply regardless of personal background.
